South Korean Politician Suggests Modern Warfare 4 as a Tool to Visualize National Security Risks

28 Oct 2026, 12:27 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Gaming Desk · Source: www.ign.com

A Call for Strategic Vigilance

In a recent development that bridges the gap between interactive media and national defense strategy, South Korean politician Han Dong-hoon has publicly urged President Lee Jae-myung to engage with the recently released video game *Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4*. Han’s recommendation is not rooted in entertainment, but rather in a desire for the administration to confront the visceral, simulated depiction of a potential North Korean invasion as a 'wake-up call' for national preparedness.

The Fiction of Seoul in Ashes

*Modern Warfare 4* features a campaign narrative that depicts a surprise attack on Seoul, characterized by an EMP strike followed by a massive conventional and technological assault. The game explores a scenario where South Korean forces find themselves struggling against an overwhelming adversary. Han Dong-hoon highlighted the harrowing imagery within the game, expressing a clear hope that the depiction of a leveled Seoul remains strictly within the domain of fiction. His core argument emphasizes that the nation must actively prepare for worst-case security contingencies rather than relying on the hope that such conflicts will never materialize.

Parallels and Geopolitical Tension

The timing of this call has drawn significant public attention due to the game's narrative structure, which includes a power struggle within North Korean leadership and the subsequent rise of the Supreme Leader’s sister to command. This fictional arc has been compared by some observers to recent real-world geopolitical tensions and rhetoric between North and South Korean leadership. While the game provides an immersive look at these dynamics, it remains a commercial entertainment product, and observers note that its depiction of military technology—such as devices capable of neutralizing defenses instantly—serves as a narrative device rather than an accurate intelligence assessment.

Context and Impact

While the suggestion has sparked conversation, it has also faced skepticism regarding the appropriateness of using a commercial video game as a pedagogical tool for high-level statecraft. Nevertheless, the move underscores the evolving influence of digital media in shaping public and political perception of security threats. The game, which received a 7/10 rating from IGN for its campaign narrative, continues to be a subject of discussion, both for its gameplay mechanics and its controversial depiction of regional conflict.
